negative_results: B10's +5 to +7% IS THE NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is a 15x miss on an expected value that came from a real measurement rather than an argument. LEVERS.md's own rule -- 'if a measurement lands more than ~2x off that estimate, fix the model before spending the next run' -- applies to F82's model, and the fix is trap 34.

TRAP 34: host time inside a driver call is NOT device-timeline time, even on a drained device. F82 bracketed each call with steady_clock and, seeing 127 of 134 issued after their own function's cudaStreamSynchronize, concluded the device was idle for their duration. 'Drained when the call STARTED' does not imply 'idle THROUGHOUT': each function issues its whole malloc batch at the TOP while the previous function's kernels -- and, inside dspark_block_forward, hc_pre and rmsnorm before the nested attn's 13 mallocs -- are still draining underneath. Only the frees genuinely follow a drain, and they are at most half the 134. The instrument that would have answered this before the build is the gap between two DEVICE events, not a host bracket. F82 declined to price its 12.99 ms of cudaStreamSynchronize as waste for exactly this reason; the error was applying that instinct to only half the data.

B10's capacity estimate was also 40x low (~5 MB predicted, 210.72 MB measured). It did not matter -- 41.2% of a 512 MB arena -- but it was wrong for a reason worth keeping: the estimate counted only the buffers named in the five draft functions and ignored that their callees' scratch was already on the arena and now stacks 3x.
controls: BIT-IDENTICAL, checked not assumed: diff over the spec token sequence, the base-AR token sequence and all 45 drafter margins against clean_post_f81.log is EMPTY. All nine verifies pair 1:1 at identical K and identical accept counts. Acceptance 2.89, first token 11111.

THE DRAFT-FREE MARKS ARE THE VARIANCE CONTROL AND THEY ALL MOVED THE OTHER WAY: cold prefill 206.1 -> 206.9 ms (+0.4%), base AR 72.3 -> 72.6 (+0.4%), warm prefill 137.1 -> 137.9 (+0.6%). The pair drawn was marginally SLOW, and the nine draft-containing marks still went 9/9 faster. That makes the -0.50% direction real; per trap 25 the magnitude still needs a second pair.

The arena LIFETIME argument (falsification step 1) was discharged by reading, then gated by the byte-identical sequence: every dkmalloc is function-local scratch consumed inside one call, no arena_reset() runs inside any of the five functions, and every buffer that crosses a reset (mkv[st], xa/xb/xemb/dout/dmarg, main_x) is raw cudaMalloc at decode.cu:646 and stays that way.

Dropping the ten per-function syncs is legal by construction: decode.cu's for(pass) loop does a blocking cudaMemcpy AND an explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize after arena_reset() and before the pass's first dkmalloc, so reset memory is drained before it is re-issued. The chain's ordering comes from being one stream, not from those syncs.
dspark_attn_forward's H2D of the stack-local hidx stays correct without its sync: cudaMemcpyAsync out of PAGEABLE host memory is specified to copy into the staging buffer before returning.
Gates unchanged at 20/20 because dmalloc/dfree/dsync fall back to raw when arena_init was never called -- and stated honestly: NO gate exercises the draft path under an arena.
